text:
marta: Heads up — hit a weird spike this morning where one org burned through burst credits and we started seeing cascading 503s from several routers. need a quick decision: 429 for per-key bursts and 503 for node/global overload, or always 429 and rely on client backoff?

sam: +1 to different signals. 429 = client-level backoff, 503 = system-level overload. we need distinct telemetry so SRE can alert appropriately.

aditya: curious how you observed the cascade? logs?

marta: timeline: a single org sent ~10k short requests in a minute. edge precheck accepted some, routers queued, but when queue length hit threshold routers started rejecting downstream with 503 to upstream callers (internal service mesh) which caused retries and amplified load.

yusuf: that explains it. retries to upstream + 503s are a death spiral. 429 with Retry-After would have given clients a chance to back off instead of retrying hard.

sam: but 429 alone can be abused — if a noisy key hits 429 and keeps sending high QPS we still thrash resources trying to parse/authorize etc. we need a small fast precheck path that can early-shed.

aditya: proposal: precheck (cheap path) returns either PASS / SOFT_SHELF / HARD_REJECT. map SOFT_SHELF -> 429 + header suggesting backoff; HARD_REJECT -> 503 for node-level. label metrics: quota.precheck_result.

marta: +1. also add `X-Quota-Burst-Remaining` and `X-Quota-Window-Reset` headers so clients and dashboard can show a live burst credit bar.

yusuf: love the header idea. Console should surface per-key burst credits and a tiny sparkline. product asked for per-route breakdown anyway.

ops-bot: deploy queued: deploy/edge-precheck-v2 started by gina — will rollout 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 30m.

gina: rollout notes: will flip on precheck fast-path that only checks token + org quota counter. no heavy auth or routing decisions. start 10% internal first.

aditya: telemetry wishlist: histogram of precheck latency, counter for precheck_result, gauge for per-router queue-depth, and fine-grained labels: org_id, route, reason (burst|rate|system). we should also emit a tracing span when we downgrade to queued response.

sam: for client behavior guidance in docs: recommend exponential backoff with jitter on 429, immediate retry on 503 only after random delay that increases with consecutive failures. make explicit that 503 likely means system-level and clients should be conservative.

yusuf: question: how long to let soft-queue stand? we can queue short tails (<=500ms) but if queued > 2s convert to 429. thoughts?

aditya: sounds fine. Implementation: queue item includes enqueue_ts; router sweeper moves items > 2s -> precheck HARD_REJECT path. minimal overhead.

marta: config snippet for policy I sketched:
```yaml
precheck:
  window_ms: 100
  max_queue_ms: 2000
  soft_threshold: 50  # concurrency
  hard_threshold: 200
  metrics_labels: [org_id, key, route, reason]
```

sam: add a `drop_reason` tag in metrics (early_shed, queue_timeout, node_overload) so alerts can route to correct oncall.

gina: rollout plan: enable headers + metrics in v1. precheck on 10% internal, watch `quota.precheck_result{reason="burst"}` and queue-depth. if error budget on 10% < 0.1% for 30m, expand.

yusuf: small UX ask: change Console to show `burst credits` and `estimated recovery time` (calc from X-Quota-Window-Reset). also show last 5 precheck outcomes in the per-key timeline.

aditya: about 429 vs 503 semantics: make them precise in our API docs: 429 = client hitting per-key/org quota or explicit soft-shed; include `Retry-After` (seconds) and `X-Quota-Burst-Remaining`. 503 = node-level or global resource exhaustion; include `Retry-After` but note no per-key credit change.

marta: testing: can we run chaos test: pick a synthetic org, blast it for 5m and verify no cross-org 503s on routers? also record metric: `cross_org_503_rate`.

sam: yes. SRE can run during low-traffic window. will add an alert when cross_org_503_rate > 0.1%.

gina: small perf note — keep precheck path <= 1ms median; otherwise it defeats purpose. use local counters and avoid RPCs.

aditya: implementation tasks: 1) precheck fast-path + metrics, 2) headers in response, 3) router queue sweeper for >2s -> 429, 4) console UX for burst credits, 5) docs for client guidance.

yusuf: who owns 3?

aditya: router team (i'll take it).

marta: ok let's ship 1,2,5 behind feature flag and start experiment. ops: watch precheck_result and queue-depth, devex: update SDKs to surface headers in next minor.

ops-bot: deploy status: deploy/edge-precheck-v2 @ 10% -> success, metrics warming.

sam: after we validate, we should consider a per-key emergency kill switch so support can instantly hard-block a noisy API key without tenant-wide impact.

gina: noted — add to support runbook.

marta: thanks all. i'll follow up with PR for the YAML policy and a short doc for SDK owners.

aditya: great thread. short action items pinned: [precheck fast-path], [headers], [router sweeper], [console telemetry], [support kill-switch].

ops-bot: reminder: incident-playbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/backpressure
